operation_details.item: The user prefers prose-only system design documents with no diagrams, sequence flows, or component boundaries.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Morning! How’s the architecture work going today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty well. I’m drafting the design for the new event-processing service.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Nice. Are you putting together the usual diagrams and sequence flows for the review?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Not this time. I prefer system design documents written entirely as prose, without diagrams, sequence flows, or explicit component boundaries.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That’s a different approach from the usual architecture template. What works better for you about prose-only documents?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: It keeps the discussion focused on behavior, tradeoffs, and operational constraints instead of making people argue over boxes and arrows.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. Are you also skipping the standard clean-code and exhaustive-testing sections?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I’m keeping the document practical and specific to the risks we actually need to address, rather than adding boilerplate sections just because they’re conventional.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that In system design documents, I want prose-only descriptions with no diagrams, sequence flows, or component boundaries.
